values: French normally uses the definite article with a body part when the reflexive pronoun already identifies the possessor.
Usually introduces an indirect question with si, pourquoi, comment, or another interrogative word: je me demande s’il viendra.
With a plural subject it can be reciprocal; the other participant may be introduced by avec.
to have an inkling of
to expect
Unlike douter de, se douter de means to suspect or anticipate that something is true rather than to doubt it.
dispose of
rid oneself of
Requires de before the person or thing removed, discarded, or escaped from.
Highlights overcoming hesitation and finally committing oneself to the action expressed by the infinitive.
Se faire + infinitive presents the subject as arranging for or undergoing the action; faire remains invariant before the infinitive.
The first faire is the conjugated causative auxiliary and the second is the infinitive meaning do or make.
The reflexive pronoun marks the affected person, so French normally uses the definite article la rather than a possessive adjective before cheville.
The spouse is introduced by avec: elle s’est mariée avec son partenaire. Se marier is normally conjugated with être in compound tenses.
Parler à quelqu’un makes the reciprocal pronoun indirect; consequently, the past participle parlé normally remains invariable.
to take place
to go on
In the impersonal question qu’est-ce qui se passe ?, the expression asks what is happening or what is wrong.
Takes à before a noun or infinitive and means to get oneself ready for an event or action.
With a plural subject the pronominal form is reciprocal and means that the participants meet one another.

batch_summary: Added reciprocity, body-part article, and causative guidance for common pronominal expressions, plus key distinctions for se douter and se passer.
